explanation.headline: Firefly Alpha met its orbit goal despite Stage 1 falling short of its ideal Δv
explanation.why: Stage 1 delivered only 2825 m/s of its ideal 4074 m/s because 977 m/s was lost to gravity, 79 m/s to drag and 194 m/s to steering; Stage 2 performed closer to ideal with 5395 m/s delivered of 5719 m/s ideal after small gravity (203 m/s), drag (1 m/s) and steering (120 m/s) losses. The combined delivered Δv of 7975 m/s was sufficient to reach the 500 km circular target (orbital speed needed ≈7612 m/s) after accounting for losses.

99001-66744-quiet.policy_text: Manoeuvre when Pc >= 1e-4 and a verified option exists. Between 1e-5 and 1e-4, or when Pc is diluted, prefer getting precise data if there is time before the latest safe burn. On public TLE data, do not decide a burn while there is time to get precise ephemeris; TLE screening finds candidates, it does not decide manoeuvres. Never manoeuvre if our propulsion status is unverified. If the other object is an active satellite that can manoeuvre, contact its operator before moving; if it is an operational satellite whose capability is unknown, notify its operator. Keep at least 30 minutes for command upload. Max 1.0 m/s per burn.

decision.rationale: Pc is 3.13e-07, well below the policy yellow threshold (1e-05) and red threshold (1e-04); with ample time (>160 h) before TCA and no urgent need to maneuver. Public TLE data precludes deciding a burn while precise ephemeris could be obtained. The other object's maneuver capability is unknown, so per policy we should notify its operator. No mission conflicts exist.
